data.name: Jeremie
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Jeremie derives from the Hebrew word yarah, which means ‘to throw.’ Jeremiah, the Biblical prophet, is believed to have received his name because God 'threw' him into the world to be a prophet. The name Jeremie is a cognate of Jeremiah.

in_hebrew.name: ירמיה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ירמיה הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'ה' יורד ומגלה את עמו'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'יר' שפירושה 'ה' יורד' ומ'יה' שפירושה 'עמו'. השם נמצא בתנ'ך ומתייחס לנביא ירמיהו, שניבא על חורבן ירושלים והגלות הבבלית. הנביא ירמיהו היה דמות מרכזית בתקופת המלכות יהודה.

in_greek.name: Ιερεμίας
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιερεμίας προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή λέξη 'ירמיה' και σημαίνει 'ο Θεός θεμελιώνει' ή 'ο Θεός ιδρύει'. Στο Χριστιανισμό, το όνομα Ιερεμίας συνδέεται με τον προφήτη Ιερεμία, ο οποίος ήταν σημαντική προσωπικότητα στην Παλαιά Διαθήκη. Ο προφήτης Ιερεμίας ήταν γνωστός για τις προφητείες του σχετικά με την πτώση της Ιερουσαλήμ και την εξορία στη Βαβυλώνα.

in_latin.name: Jeremie
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Jeremie is derived from the Hebrew name 'ירמיה' and means 'the Lord establishes' or 'the Lord sets up'. In Christian tradition, the name Jeremie is associated with the prophet Jeremiah, who was a major figure in the Old Testament. The prophet Jeremiah was known for his prophecies about the fall of Jerusalem and the Babylonian exile. The name Jeremie has been used in various forms throughout history, including in Latin as 'Jeremias'.

in_english.name: Jeremie
in_english.long_meaning: The name Jeremie is of Hebrew origin, derived from 'ירמיה' (Yirmeyahu), meaning 'the Lord establishes' or 'the Lord appoints'. It is associated with the prophet Jeremiah, a significant figure in the Old Testament known for his prophecies about the fall of Jerusalem and the Babylonian exile. The name Jeremie has been used in Christian tradition to signify a person who is chosen or appointed by God. It symbolizes divine establishment and purpose.

biblical_reference.note: The prophet Jeremiah was a major figure in the Old Testament, known for his prophecies about the fall of Jerusalem and the Babylonian exile.

data.cultural_impact: Jeremie is a name deeply rooted in the cultural heritage and religious traditions of the Jewish and Christian communities. Throughout history, the name has carried significant weight as a reminder of the Biblical prophet's unwavering faith and commitment to conveying God's message to the world.
data.spiritual_significance: Named after the revered prophet Jeremiah, Jeremie is believed to carry strong spiritual significance. His namesake serves as an inspiration to those who bear it, with the message to uncompromisingly follow God's will, and to be brave and steadfast in spreading the Word of God, just as Jeremiah did. The name continues to carries the resonance of a deep spiritual heritage and a reminder of the prophetic tradition within the Judeo-Christian religious tradition.

historical_references.reference: Jeremiah was a prophet in the Old Testament of the Bible, active during the late 6th and early 5th centuries BCE.
